newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sanyo, NTV develop 3D digital broadcast system.
newsitem.headline: Sanyo, NTV develop 3D digital broadcast system.

text.p: Japan's Sanyo Electric Co Ltd and Nippon Television Network Corp (NTV) said on Tuesday they had developed a new system for broadcasting 3D images and would start test transmissions later this year.
The system uses progressive-scan technology developed by NTV and requires viewers to have decoders in their TV sets as well as special glasses to see the three-dimensional images.

The two firms said they planned to launch test broadcasts this summer to gauge the commercial possibilities of the technology. But they said details of the scale of the investment and possible timing of the start of commercial 3D broadcasts had yet to be decided.

Under the system, broadcasters will combine right-eye and left-eye images into one signal that will be transmitted using progressive scan technology and broken down into the two images again by the decoder.

NTV, a nationwide broadcaster, announced the development of digital progressive-scan technology in January last year. The technology is a way of broadcasting images in a more computer-compatible way than the interlace method currently used for most television broadcasting.
